welcome.label: Welcome · Zippy vs Scoot

parts.label: 🤖 Rosa’s question
parts.title: Should she trade Scoot?
parts.body: Zippy went farther. Does that make Zippy faster?

parts.label: 🔍 Today
parts.title: Measure speed
parts.body: How far, how long, and a fair test.

welcome.script:
(Hold up a paper sign that says FASTEST!) If I hold up a sign that says fastest, does that make me fast?

[ON SCREEN: Zippy’s sign]
The hot-dog stand’s robot, Zippy, has a sign like this. Ninety steps!

[ON SCREEN: Rosa’s question]
Rosa wants to know: should she trade Scoot for Zippy?

[ON SCREEN: Today]
Today you’ll find out what it takes to PROVE who is faster. Read the case file just below me. Look closely at the tickets.

warmup.label: Warm-Up · fix the sign (Clue 1)

parts.label: 🧲 Fix the sign
parts.title: Word magnets
rows: Drag a magnet onto the blank

warmup.script:
(Take three giant steps across the room.) Three steps! Was I fast? Hmm, you can’t tell. I didn’t say how long it took.

[ON SCREEN: Fix the sign]
Zippy’s sign has the same problem. Drag a word magnet onto each blank so the sign only says what the number proves.

[ON SCREEN: Far or fast?]
Are ninety steps about how far, or how fast? Then answer three quick lines about races you have seen.

part1.label: Part 1 · scratch-off tickets (Clue 2)
part1.script:
(Cover one hand with the other, like hiding a number.) I ran thirty feet. Am I fast? I’m not telling you the time!

[ON SCREEN: Scratch-off tickets]
Each ticket hides a number under silver. Call the race first. It’s okay to say you can’t tell yet. Then rub off the silver and call it again.

part2.label: Part 2 · slice it into seconds (Clue 3)

parts.label: 🧮 Zippy and Scoot
parts.title: 90 steps in 90 s · 60 steps in 30 s

part2.script:
(Hold up a long strip of paper and fold it into equal parts.) If I cut a race into equal pieces of time, I can compare the pieces.

[ON SCREEN: Zippy and Scoot]
Zippy went ninety steps in ninety seconds. Scoot went sixty steps in thirty. Both numbers are different! So who is faster?

[ON SCREEN: Slice it into seconds]
Press Run. Every ten seconds, press Cut. Then compare one piece from each robot.

[ON SCREEN: The photo finish]
After that, a camera that takes a picture of TIME. Wow.

explore.label: Part 3 · the fair rematch (Clue 4)

parts.label: 🏁 The fair rematch
parts.title: One start, one finish
rows: Drag the finish flag onto the tape
Start the race, read both clocks
Type your numbers in the table

explore.script:
(Draw a start line and a finish line in the air with your finger.) Same start. Same finish. Same floor. Now it’s a fair race!

[ON SCREEN: The fair rematch]
Drag the finish flag onto the tape, or tap a mark. Start the race and watch both race clocks. Then type each robot’s distance and time into your data table. Press Check, and your claim sentence builds itself from YOUR numbers.

assignment.label: Assignment · crack the case

parts.label: 🔓 Crack the case
parts.title: Which robot is really faster?
parts.body: Pick the answer that fits all four clues.

parts.label: ✍️ Your case report
parts.title: Three places to work
rows: Race two things and draw your data table

assignment.script:
[ON SCREEN: Crack the case]
You have four clues. So which robot is really faster, and how do you know? Pick the answer that fits every clue. Then fill in Rosa’s report, and watch out for a twist!

[ON SCREEN: Your case report]
Next: two short answers. Then race two things at home, or use your rematch numbers, and draw your data table. Then sketch and label it. Last comes your CER.

evidence.label: Use your evidence · CER

parts.label: 💬 The claim
parts.title: A classmate says…
parts.body: “You can tell which car is fastest just by watching them. You don’t need to time it.”

parts.label: 🧩 The planner
parts.title: Claim · Evidence · Reasoning
rows: Tap I agree or I disagree.

evidence.script:
(Squint and point at two imaginary cars.) That one’s faster. I can tell just by looking! Can I, though?

[ON SCREEN: The claim]
A classmate says watching is enough. Think about Zippy’s sign, the photo finish and the race clocks.

[ON SCREEN: The planner]
Tap your side and two facts. Then explain how they prove your claim. Try starting with “This shows that…”

closing.label: Case closed

parts.label: 🪧 Your specimen
parts.title: Zippy’s sign
parts.body: Finish the checklist to stamp CASE CLOSED.

closing.script:
(Hold up the FASTEST sign, cross out the word and write FARTHER.) There. Now the sign tells the truth.

[ON SCREEN: Your specimen]
Finish your checklist, and Zippy’s sign goes into your Field Notebook.

[ON SCREEN: Confetti]

[ON SCREEN: Next lesson]
Next time: waves. How can energy travel across the water, while the water itself mostly stays put?

quiz.label: Self-Check
quiz.script: Quick check: three questions, one at a time. It’s not graded. If you miss one, read the hint and try again.
